 Policy
 Permit Parking and Parking Consultation Policy

 1. PURPOSE

 Strathfield Council is the parking authority for all on-street parking within the Strathfield Local
 Government Area (LGA). Under the Road Transport (General) Regulation 2024 parking
 authorities may issue a permit authorising the parking of a vehicle without charge or time
 restrictions in a parking space located within a parking area or road.
 In certain areas where demand for on-street parking exceeds supply, or areas which fall
 under Council’s Public Parking Strategy, Council may introduce time restricted parking to
 better manage these facilities.
 To allow residents, residents’ visitors, business to park their vehicles in these restricted areas
 without time restrictions or charge, Council has implemented a Permit Parking Scheme
 (RPS).
 This Policy outlines the circumstances under which individuals or organisations may apply for,
 and be granted, a Parking Permit. Permits will only be issued in accordance with the eligibility
 criteria and conditions outlined in this Policy.

 Consultation on Proposed Parking Changes
 Consultation for localised parking area changes is undertaken to a 25.0m radius.
 Consultation for a change to a parking scheme area requires the entire area to be consulted.
 Consultation is for a minimum of 28 days. If the consultation period falls during the school
 holidays, then the consultation period is extended by a minimum of two weeks

 a) Consultation is undertaken via a letterbox Drop for smaller areas.
 b) For larger consultation areas a QR code is also included to allow people to access
 the Council’s website.

 More information, including a map of eligible properties, is available from Council’s Customer
 Service Centre and website. www.Strathfield.nsw.gov.au

 2. SCOPE
 Strathfield Council offers four types of Parking Permit for use by members of the public:
  Resident Permit
  Visitor Permit
  Business Permit (Homebush West Only)
  Temporary Visitor Permit
 Permits may only be issued as outlined within the Policy. In order to ensure the number of
 permits issued in an RPS area does not exceed the available on-street parking in that RPS
 area Council must set a limit on the number of permits residents and businesses are eligible
 to receive.

 Each Parking Permit is valid for a fixed period and is issued for a specific Permit Area only (as
 indicated on both the street signage).

 Parking Permits will NOT be issued for trucks (vehicles over 4.5 tonnes GVM), trailers even if
 they are attached to a vehicle with a permit. Also if they are boats or caravans, buses, trams,
 tractors or any other vehicle deemed unsuitable by the General Manager.

 6. POLICY APPLICATION

 6.1 Resident Permits



 Resident parking permits enable eligible residents, who do not have sufficient on-site parking,
 to park on-street and avoid time limits and parking fees. The number of permits available to
 each property is based upon the number of off-street parking spaces available.


 Specific entitlements are:

 Number of Off-Street Car Spaces Number of Permits

 Two per Household 2

 Visitor 1


 Off-street parking spaces are defined as a garage, carport, or any other facility which allows a
 resident to store their vehicle within or on their premises. All applications will be assessed and
 audited individually for off-street car spaces.

 Resident Permits will only be issued for vehicles that are registered at the address of the
 applicant or (for business vehicles that are used privately) kept at the resident’s address.
 Resident Permits are linked to a vehicle’s registration and therefore are non-transferable.

 Premises including, but no limited to, boarding houses, hostels, seniors housing and bed and
 breakfast accommodation will be assessed based on the number of off-street parking spaces
 available, with eligibility to be determined by authorised Council Officers.

 Properties outside of residential flat buildings which are not subdivided, including properties
 with granny flats or secondary dwellings, will be treated as single property and not entitled to
 any additional permits for occupants beyond the above provisions.

 New multi-dwelling developments (such as residential flat buildings, townhouses and mixed
 use developments) in existing Permit Parking Scheme Areas will be excluded from eligibility
 to obtain permits. Such developments are required to provide on-site parking is accordance
 with Council’s DCP or relevant planning Policy.


 All Resident parking permits are valid for two (2) years from the date of application being
 approved.

 6.2 Visitor Permits


 To allow eligible residents’ visitors such as carers, relatives, friends, medical practitioners and
 tradespersons to park on-street in certain locations without restriction or charge, Council may
 issue Visitor Permits. Eligible residents are entitled to a maximum of two Visitor Permits as
 follows:

 • One free Visitor Permit per household.

 • One additional Visitor Permit with a fee payable in accordance with Council’s
 Schedule of Fees and Charges.

 Visitor Parking Permits are for residents’ visitors only and cannot be issued for business or
 organisation. Visitor Permits are only valid in circumstances where the driver or passenger of
 the vehicle are directly visiting the address of the applicant (resident)

 The first visitor permit is provided free of charge with an annual fee payable for an additional
 Visitor Permit. Lost Visitor Permits are replaceable at a cost, in accordance with Council’s
 Schedule of Fees and Charges. Pensioner Concession Card holders are exempt from fees in
 relation to Visitor permits.

 Premises including, but no limited to, boarding houses, hostels, seniors housing and bed and
 breakfast accommodation will be assessed based on the number of off-street parking spaces
 available, with eligibility to be determined by authorised Council Officers.


 All Visitor parking permits are valid for one (1) year from the date of application being approved.




 6.3 Business Permits


 Business Permits allow for owners or operators of commercial premises who pay Business
 Rates and are located within a Permit Parking Homebush Town Centre areas only, that
 have nil off-street parking spaces, to park on-street without restriction or charge. All costs are
 in accordance with Council’s Schedule of Fees and Charges.


 Business Permits are only available to an eligible vehicle being required for routine use in the
 day to day operation of the registered business and where the vehicle is registered for
 business use in the name of the business.

 area of visitation or service.
 The permits may be requested by members of the Executive Team and may be approved at
 the discretion of the General Manager on a case-by-case basis.

 7. Requests for Additional Parking Permits

 In instances where an applicant requests an additional Resident Permit, over and above the
 maximum allowable under this Policy, an assessment is to take place by the Manager Traffic
 and Transport, with sign-off to occur by the Manager Engineering.

 This assessment will be based on, but not limited to, the following factors:
  the area for which the Parking Permit is to be issued
  the total number of Parking Permits issued for the area in which the Parking Permit is
 sought
  the total number of Parking Permits (in all categories) that have been issued to the
 applicant
  the total number of off-street parking spaces within the property or available to the
 applicant
  the total number of vehicles registered to the address
  the individual circumstances identified by the applicant as being necessary for the
 additional Parking Permit(s)

 A maximum of one additional Resident permit may be issued above what is permissible the
 provisions in Section 2.1.

 The decision to refuse or allow additional Parking Permit(s), over and above the maximum
 allowable, and the reasons for this decision, must be sufficiently documented. The reasons for
 refusing or allowing additional Parking Permit(s) must be provided to the applicant.




 8. Special Consideration
 Applications may be made under special consideration for temporary one-day permits to be
 issued to facilitate religious events, such as weddings and funerals etc. A formal application
 (together with supporting documentation) must be made to Council in advance of any event for
 assessment. Applications will be assessed by the Manager Traffic and Transport, with sign-off to
 occur by the Manager Engineering.
 This assessment will be based on, but not limited to, the following factors:
 • parking demand within the requested area
 • potential impacts upon the road network
 • history of request for special consideration

 9. Conditions of Use for All Parking Permits
 Digital parking e-Permits are a digital permit that will be associated to a vehicle’s registration.
 Permit holders will no longer receive a physical permit that needs to be displayed in a vehicle:


 a) Parking Permits exempt vehicles from time limits and parking charges ONLY in locations
 signposted as "Permit Holders Excepted (Area Identifier)".
 b) It is the responsibility of the driver to ensure the permit is valid and used correctly.
 c) A valid parking permit exempts the nominated vehicle (by registration number) from
 timed restrictions only in the applicable Zone only. All other restrictions (in accordance
 with Road Rules 2014) still apply.
 d) Parking permits are not available, nor valid if the e-Permit is assigned to boat trailers, box
 trailers, caravans or vehicle over 4.5 Tonne. (in line with the Permit Parking Scheme
 policy).
 e) Parking Permit holders are strictly prohibited from selling, leasing, transferring or
 assigning any Parking Permit to any party for any use not permitted under this Policy.
 f) If a Parking Permit holder disposes of the vehicle to which the Permit applies, and/or
 changes their residential address, the permit holder is responsible for the cancelation of
 the Permit and its return to Council (for printed permits).
 g) Fraudulent use of a Parking Permit is an offence and may result in fines or the
 cancellation of the Parking Permit.
 h) All Parking Permits remain the property of Strathfield Council and Council reserves the
 right to withdraw and cancel any Parking Permit that is used in contravention to this
 Policy.


 10. Application/Renewal Process and Forms
 Residents and Business operators of Homebush Town Centre areas only wanting to obtain a
 Parking Permit must complete the online application form. The vehicles registration certificate,
 personal identification and other relevant documentation must be attached for review.
 Applications will be assessed, and eligibility confirmed, by Council Officers prior to the issuing of
 the Parking Permit(s).
 Where applicable, fees must be paid upon submission of the application form. If an application is
 unsuccessful, except in the case of fraudulent applications, Council will refund the fee in full.
 Permit holders will be notified prior to the expiration of their current Parking Permit/s. Fees and
 Charges will be updated annually in accordance with Council’s Schedule of Fees and Charges.
 If you have any queries regarding Council’s Permit Parking Scheme, please contact our
 Customer Service Centre on (02) 9748 9999 or email Council@Strathfield.nsw.gov.au

 6.5 Town Centres and Civic Spaces - Proposed Line Marking of Parking Bays

 Background

 Council previously received a request to consider line marking of parking spaces in the town centres and
 civic spaces around the LGA to better delineate parking spaces and prevent vehicles parking such that an
 additional parking space is removed.


 Report

 This request was originally discouraged by Council as this would likely decrease available parking in the town
 centres. Australian Standard 2890.5 for on-street parking requires the following parking space lengths:

 • 5.4m for an end space unobstructed on at least one side

 • 6.3m for end spaces with an obstruction on the side not adjacent to another parking space

 • 6.0m for intermediate spaces between two other parking spaces

 These lengths may be increased where turnover is high and/or larger vehicles like vans frequently access the
 parking spaces.

 Many private vehicles are 4.5m-5.0m in length, representative of a B85 vehicle (vehicle of the 85th percentile
 length) such as a sedan or small SUV. Consequently, these vehicles can often park using less space than the
 lengths above, resulting in the ability to store more vehicles in a length of road where using the above
 lengths would decrease parking availability when considering most vehicles.

 However, Council have recently observed the following at several locations:

 • Vehicles parking and leaving a significant gap in excess of 1.0m to the next vehicle such that this
 detracts from the available space of the remaining length of parking area and prevents another
 parking space being used; or

 • A ‘vehicle shift’ phenomenon that develops over the course of the day. Initially, vehicles park close
 to each other, leaving enough room for adjacent vehicles to exit the space but parking closely
 enough to maximise the parking spaces in that section of parking.


 Over time as different size vehicles arrive and leave driven by different people with varying tolerances
 of gaps between vehicles, the location of each initial parking space moves such that at varying points
 throughout the day, 1-2 parking spaces in that section may be temporarily removed due to the way the
 vehicles are currently parked.

 This may be exacerbated when motorbikes park between cars or a car needs a larger space to access
 their boot such that the gaps between parked vehicles increases further.

 So, while Council’s initial hesitation to avoid the line marking of these high-demand parking areas was to
 retain more parking overall, the line marking is required to clearly indicate parking areas to vehicles such that
 all parking spaces are maintained throughout the day.

 However, the line marking will only be implemented for sections that closely align with required parking bay
 lengths. Where parking sections are of a length that line marking to the minimum required lengths would
 leave a half-space, these spaces will not be line marked as:
 • In the worst-case scenario, uncontrolled parking would likely result in the same number of parking
 spaces being available as line marked spaces

 • In the best-case scenario, each vehicle would be parked in a way that sacrifices 200-400mm from
 each space to provide an additional parking space
